title: A cheaper model, backed by evidence
narration: Refund extraction looks simple, until the model picks the wrong date. RouteWise helps developers choose a cheaper model setup, backed by evidence.

title: Fix the missing date
narration: Here’s a recorded synthetic example. The old route misses the refund date. RouteWise reads “this Friday” against the store’s timestamp, and gets April twenty-fourth.

title: Hold ambiguous answers for review
narration: If the date is ambiguous, it holds the answer for review. You can inspect the source, raw response, and every check.

title: Set your requirements
narration: Choose your accuracy and response-time targets. RouteWise compares NVIDIA Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory, then picks the cheapest setup the evidence supports. On three hundred twelve synthetic conversations, this setup completed ninety-eight point four percent correctly without review, with no incorrect answers released.

title: Let the evidence decide
narration: Need a faster response? The recommendation switches to Super. Ask for more certainty than the data supports, and it recommends nothing.

title: Inspect a real API call
narration: This call was captured while recording. Nano leaves the date blank; RouteWise resolves it to April sixth. The trace includes the actual response time and every model-call charge.

title: See the projected cost
narration: At a million requests a month, recorded inference costs project to about eighty dollars, versus three hundred forty-nine for Super. Hosting and human review cost extra.

title: Export the decision
narration: Download the decision and integration recipe. These results use synthetic data. Independent human validation is still pending, and the latest noise test missed its response-time target. RouteWise shows those limits alongside its recommendation.
